documented_probe: Real upstream tree apache/commons-lang@9d1f110190081801754a8a0b447693ad2407a502 (parent of the upstream fix 10f4421456b891d5a426348511383f387c99f3e1 for issue #1769), shallow-fetched in the Dockerfile, detached at the parent so the fix commit is out of reach, with the offline Maven repository at /opt/m2repo warmed and the module compiled at build time. Seeded symptom: Fraction.multiplyBy throws ArithmeticException 'overflow: mulPos' for the valid computation -1/46341 * 100/1000000 = -1/463410000 because the Knuth 4.5.1 cross-gcd cancels factors only across the two operands and assumes both are reduced; divideBy and pow route through the same code. The agent gets an executable repro (/app/probe.sh + FractionProbe.java), the symptom description, and the project's own maven test commands, but no file name and no issue/commit reference.
notes: Easy SWE-bench-shaped debugging task on a real upstream JVM library. The fix is a small, self-contained rewrite of the multiplyBy cross-gcd block inside one method; the upstream regression assertions added by the fix commit (testMultiply and testDivide additions) are extracted at image build time into /opt/golden/FractionTest.java and never committed here. The verifier requires the agent's tree to still sit at the pinned parent with exactly one commit object and the fix commit unreachable, runs the direct repro, the golden tests, the project's own test classes (FractionTest, FractionReadObjectTest, NumberUtilsTest, IEEE754rUtilsTest), and three authored hidden-case classes that use inputs the upstream test does not: both-unreduced near-limit products (12/556092 * 125/5792500), unreduced-divisor quotients with negative and prime-denominator variants, a pow(2) of an unreduced fraction, and guards that genuinely overflowing products still throw and that zero/identity/sign/reduced-operand behaviour is unchanged. Expected values in the hidden cases are computed independently with BigInteger. difficulty_guess from the issue pool was 'easy'. The oracle applies the same fix the upstream commit ships and re-proves the repro, the golden tests, and the project's own math tests. The maven repo and JDK are the same versions the mining container used (maven 3.9.9 from archive.apache.org, openjdk-21-jdk).
